scope.description: Decision-pass change review against actual immediate parent 06-change-review, retaining deep web/API scope and stable scenario identities.
in_scope: Browser application, application origin, OIDC login, server-side session and bearer-token admission
Private API resource, operation and property authorization
Report views and PDF, CSV and JSON exports
Durable asynchronous ingestion, repository analysis, correction, delivery and recovery reached through web/API operations
GitHub, source, identity, AI and notification adapters and their responses
PostgreSQL persistence, audit history and security-event obligations
Rendering of publisher text, evidence, company notes, identifiers and errors
out_of_scope: Implementation defects, runtime behavior and deployment claims
Public APIs, public feeds, native mobile clients and native password or recovery flows
Inbound notification-provider callbacks and public webhooks, which FR-10.13 excludes
User file uploads and upload preview/download flows, which the release does not define

Optional method executions and risk scoring without a supplied rubric
objectives: Prevent unauthorized company, resource, function and property access across UI, API, exports and jobs
Preserve intended browser request authority, session transitions and current roles
Keep provider and repository content inert, bounded and unable to direct execution
Prevent private evidence, credentials and company context from crossing unapproved output or provider boundaries
Preserve durable work identity, revocation, correction and failure semantics without duplicate effects
Keep audit and security-event claims distinct from emission, persistence, detection and alert delivery
assumptions: The five supplied specifications describe the intended release, not implemented behavior.

threats.scenario: A party able to induce an authenticated browser request causes a cookie-authenticated mutation that the user did not intend if a state-changing route lacks effective session-bound CSRF and configured-origin enforcement.
threats.objective: Preserve intended browser authority for mutations.
prerequisites: The target operation accepts ambient browser session authority.
The attacker can cause the authenticated browser to submit the operation.
The concrete route omits or misapplies the required CSRF/origin checks.
actor_assumptions: Can influence a user's browser to make a request but does not possess the session secret.
Knows or can infer the state-changing operation and accepted fields.
threats.confidence_rationale: The browser mutation surface and required countercontrol are explicit, but no route inventory or implementation exists. C-WEB-REQUEST would defeat the scenario if implemented for every mutation; route-level enforcement evidence would decide it.

threats.scenario: A session or cached authorization remains usable after logout, role removal, issuer/mapping change or privilege transition, allowing stale access or leaving private company data visible after authority is lost.
threats.objective: Make identity, role and displayed private state follow current authority transitions.
prerequisites: A valid session or displayed private response predates an authority transition.
Session/configuration revision or role freshness is not rechecked within the specified bound, or old browser state is not cleared.
The stale context can reach a protected read or operation.
actor_assumptions: Previously held valid user or admin authority.
Can replay an old session context or continue using an already open browser view.
threats.confidence_rationale: The specifications explicitly require invalidation, bounded freshness and UI clearing, which are strong counterclaims but not implementation evidence. Session-transition and browser-storage tests would decide the scenario.

threats.scenario: A valid user changes an object identifier, invokes an admin function through an alternate API route, or supplies/receives unauthorized properties to alter another user's personal settings or privileged shared state.
threats.objective: Preserve object, function, property, personal-owner and admin authorization across UI and API routes.
prerequisites: The caller has valid authentication but lacks the required owner or admin permission.
An alternate identifier, function or property reaches a use case.
The use case relies on submitted ownership/role data or an unscoped lookup/projection.
actor_assumptions: Is an admitted company user able to call private API operations.
Can modify identifiers, requested functions or writable/readable properties.
threats.confidence_rationale: The differentiated user/admin and personal-owner model makes this scenario concrete. C-AUTHZ and C-VALIDATION are explicit countercontrols; the missing per-operation matrix and implementation keep it a hypothesis.

threats.scenario: An export selected while access was valid is generated or retrieved after role loss, archive, source-use restriction or report-scope change, or a caller-controlled result identifier resolves to an export that is no longer permitted to that caller.
threats.objective: Keep export creation, retained result and download authority current and resource-bound.
prerequisites: Export selection and execution or retrieval occur at different times.
Authority or source-use state changes, or the result identifier is caller-influenced.
The worker/download path trusts enqueue-time authority or identifier possession without current scoped authorization.
actor_assumptions: Can create or observe an export job/result identifier while authorized, or can alter a candidate identifier.
Later lacks current permission for the report or retained content.
threats.confidence_rationale: Challenge narrowed cross-user ownership because every admitted user may read active company reports; the relevant loss paths are role/session loss, archive/source-rights change and identifier-bound access to noncurrent output. Creation and retrieval remain separate explicit flows, G-004 remains open, and no end-to-end authority evidence defeats the hypothesis.

threats.scenario: Publisher text, company or vendor names, company notes, file/evidence excerpts or model output is interpreted as active browser content in another user's or administrator's view.
threats.objective: Render every untrusted content source inertly while preserving the restricted note format.
prerequisites: Attacker-influenced content reaches a rendered view.
A renderer, preview or later transformation bypasses the shared inert/restricted representation.
The receiving browser executes or applies active content in the application origin.
actor_assumptions: Can influence an ingested source, proposed vendor/company-visible string, company note through an authorized admin account, repository evidence or model output.
Targets a user or admin who views the stored content.
threats.confidence_rationale: Multiple specified untrusted text sources cross into privileged views. C-OUTPUT and C-UNTRUSTED-DATA explicitly counter the scenario, but no renderer or transformation evidence exists.

threats.scenario: A private report, repository excerpt or company context is reused by an intermediary for a signed-out client or remains in a browser profile after signout/role loss and is exposed outside the current authorized session.
threats.objective: Prevent private response reuse outside the authorized session and clear private client state after authority loss.
prerequisites: A private response or derived view is cached or persisted beyond the authorized context.
A signed-out or later unauthorized context can receive or display the stored response.
No-store, browser-storage prohibition or session-loss clearing is absent or ineffective.
actor_assumptions: Can access the same intermediary cache or browser profile after the authorized session.
Does not otherwise have current permission to the private content.
threats.confidence_rationale: Challenge removed an unsupported same-company cross-user distinction because admitted users broadly share report visibility. Signed-out/intermediary reuse and stale browser-profile display remain supported privacy boundaries. No-store and client clearing are protective claims, but G-006 records the missing runtime observation.

threats.scenario: An admin-configured source/provider/destination URL or a redirect causes an outbound adapter to connect to an unapproved internal, metadata, alternate-origin or attacker-controlled destination.
threats.objective: Constrain every outbound connection to its purpose-specific approved destination and address policy.
prerequisites: A configurable URL, provider discovery result or redirect influences an outbound destination.
Socket-level address and redirect validation is missing, bypassed or weaker on retry.
The service network can reach a prohibited target or forwards credentials/payload to it.
actor_assumptions: Can influence an admin-configured integration/source value, source redirect or provider response.
Knows a target reachable from the service network.
threats.confidence_rationale: Configurable retrieval and provider adapters make the boundary concrete. C-EGRESS is unusually detailed counterevidence, but it is only a required control without transport evidence.

threats.scenario: A source, AI or delivery-provider response field is trusted as business authority, allowing untrusted data or an acknowledgment to alter finding, delivery, configuration or workflow state beyond its defined meaning.
threats.objective: Keep external response data typed, bounded and non-authoritative except through an explicit local policy transition.
prerequisites: An external response contains attacker/provider-influenced fields.
The adapter passes fields beyond its validated schema or semantic contract.
A downstream owner treats the response as permission, human readership, definite evidence or authorization to change business state.
actor_assumptions: Controls or can influence an external payload or compromised provider response.
Cannot directly call the internal state transition but can shape the response consumed by it.
threats.confidence_rationale: Challenge found explicit counterevidence for delivery semantics: provider acceptance is not readership and model/source content remains untrusted. The hypothesis is therefore narrowed to absent adapter-specific response-field and downstream-authority contracts captured by G-005; those contracts and negative tests would decide it.

threats.scenario: A queued or running job performs a repository read, issue write, notification, AI request or result commit after repository access, source rights, recipient authority or resource state was revoked, or after its lease was superseded.
threats.objective: Make delayed work obey current authority and fencing at every effect and commit.
prerequisites: Work is admitted before an authority/resource-state change or lease expiry.
The worker trusts queued context or stale attempt state.
No current authorization/resource-state check and fencing token protects the external effect or commit.
actor_assumptions: Can trigger or wait for a legitimate delayed workflow, or cause revocation/archive while it is pending.
May control a stale worker attempt or exploit timing without direct database authority.
threats.confidence_rationale: The architecture explicitly contains delayed work and revocation/archive transitions. C-JOBS and C-AUTHZ directly counter the scenario, but no implementation or recovery evidence exists.

threats.scenario: A timeout, crash or unknown provider outcome is blindly retried, creating duplicate notifications, issue updates, external AI charges or other effects, or recording a false success/failure state.
threats.objective: Preserve one logical operation across retries and distinguish unknown, provider acceptance and human outcome.
prerequisites: An external effect may have occurred but its result is unknown.
A retry is issued without stable effect identity, provider reconciliation or effect-specific idempotency.
The provider or local owner does not safely deduplicate the attempt.
actor_assumptions: Can induce timeout, connection loss, crash or delayed provider response.
Benefits from duplicate or inconsistent external effects but need not compromise provider credentials.
threats.confidence_rationale: The requirements explicitly distinguish unknown outcomes and demand reconciliation, demonstrating the relevant invariant. C-JOBS is counterevidence only at specification level; restart and provider-reconciliation tests would decide it.

threats.scenario: Large, deeply nested, highly expanded or numerous HTTP/source/repository/export inputs exhaust event-loop, worker, memory, database, disk or provider capacity and delay interactive or durable work.
threats.objective: Maintain bounded availability and visible backlog under untrusted and high-volume work.
prerequisites: An actor or provider can supply data or request work near an exposed processing boundary.
One or more byte, depth, expansion, concurrency, time, queue or temporary-storage limits is absent or ineffective.
Shared capacity is consumed before cancellation, shedding or bounded failure.
actor_assumptions: Can make authorized API/export requests or influence source/repository content.
Can repeat work within whatever admission limits exist.
threats.confidence_rationale: High-volume repository/source/export processing and conservative budgets are specified, making availability exposure concrete. C-VALIDATION, C-UNTRUSTED-DATA and C-EGRESS would constrain it; no load or adversarial parser evidence exists.

threats.scenario: Private repository/company identifiers or sensitive snippets cross the AI boundary, or returned model evidence identifiers resolve outside the authorized assessment and contaminate a finding.
threats.objective: Keep AI egress minimized and local evidence authority assessment-scoped.
prerequisites: An assessment invokes the optional external AI provider.
Final serialized bytes bypass or outgrow the allowlisted projection, or returned references are accepted without local scoped resolution.
The result is persisted, displayed or delivered as supported advice/evidence.
actor_assumptions: Can influence repository/source/model text or provider response.
May attempt to include private identifiers or invented/cross-assessment evidence references.
threats.confidence_rationale: The specifications explicitly call out final-byte gating, placeholders and scoped reference resolution, which makes both failure modes concrete and supplies countercontrols. Captured-byte and cross-assessment tests are absent; AI digest auditing is blocked.

threats.scenario: A notification, shared Slack message or public GitHub issue is sent to an unauthorized destination or includes private company/repository evidence because current destination access, source rights or public-evidence classification is not rechecked.
threats.objective: Prevent external output from disclosing private or rights-restricted information.
prerequisites: A finding, correction or report is eligible for external delivery.
Destination authority, recipient access, source rights or public/private classification changes or is evaluated incorrectly.
The output projection includes fields not permitted for that channel/destination.
actor_assumptions: Can influence destination/routing configuration, report content or resource lifecycle, or is a former recipient.
Can observe the external channel or public issue.
threats.confidence_rationale: The product explicitly supports private data, shared Slack and public issue output, and requires immediate rechecks. C-OUTPUT, C-AUTHZ and C-JOBS are countercontrols, but no channel-specific projection or delivery evidence exists.

threats.scenario: A denied, failed, rolled-back or AI-egress action cannot be durably recorded, independently observed or represented under the closed event schema, leaving administrators unable to investigate or distinguish silence from health.
threats.objective: Preserve trustworthy accountability and bounded detection for security-relevant actions and pipeline failure.
prerequisites: A required event occurs outside the atomic administrative transaction, or requires the unresolved AI digest field.
No approved durable path/destination/consumer or independent silence monitor is available.
Ordinary telemetry emission fails, drops or cannot represent the obligation.
actor_assumptions: Can trigger a denied/failed/rolled-back security-relevant action or exploit an operational outage.
Benefits from reduced investigation evidence without needing to alter the business record.
threats.confidence_rationale: OD-001 through OD-005 explicitly acknowledge unresolved representation, destination and durability obligations; this is a supported design gap, not a claim that events are currently lost. C-AUDIT preserves the intended contract but cannot close the decisions.

threats.scenario: Concurrent or retried privileged edits overwrite a newer repository/source/connector/OIDC configuration, activate stale authority, or commit a mutation without the matching audit/configuration revision.
threats.objective: Preserve privileged configuration invariants and accountability under concurrency and retry.
prerequisites: Two administrators or a retry operate on the same configuration/resource revision.
The mutation does not bind authorization and expected revision in one scoped transaction or equivalent lock/constraint.
A stale write can become active or audit/work intent does not commit atomically with it.
actor_assumptions: Has legitimate admin access or can replay an admin operation after an uncertain response.
Can create a concurrent update but does not require database privileges.
threats.confidence_rationale: The API defines 409 conflicts and security rules require version/locking and atomic audit, so the invariant is concrete. No operation-specific commitment/precondition matrix or transaction implementation exists.

threats.scenario: Malformed, ambiguous, contradictory or incomplete source/repository evidence is accepted as a definite match or clean result, corrupting findings and suppressing needed follow-up.
threats.objective: Preserve evidence integrity and explicit uncertainty in exposure determinations.
prerequisites: Untrusted evidence is malformed, ambiguous, unsupported, truncated or contradictory.
Validation/comparison/coverage policy silently normalizes or drops the uncertainty.
The assessment emits a definite exposure or clean result without the required evidence.
actor_assumptions: Can influence a source or repository artifact, or relies on naturally incomplete provider evidence.
Benefits from a false clean, false definite match or obscured coverage gap.
threats.confidence_rationale: The product requirements repeatedly forbid unsupported definite or clean results, demonstrating a central integrity invariant. C-UNTRUSTED-DATA and the supplied requirements counter it; parser/comparator implementation evidence is absent.

threats.scenario: Restoring database/configuration state reactivates obsolete sessions, queued effects or connector credentials before current destinations, rights and keys are revalidated.
threats.objective: Keep restored installations quarantined until authority and external effects are explicitly re-established.
prerequisites: A backup restores business state, session/work records and encrypted connector references.
Startup resumes service, jobs or connectors without the specified quarantine gate.
Old sessions, destinations, access grants or credentials are no longer authorized.
actor_assumptions: Can influence restore sequencing or exploit a restored stale session/effect.
May be a former authorized recipient or principal rather than a database administrator.
threats.confidence_rationale: Restore quarantine is a specified control and ledger subject, so the transition is concrete. No restore implementation or exercise exists; C-AUTHN, C-SECRETS-AI, C-JOBS and C-AUDIT would jointly defeat it.

controls.description: OIDC code/PKCE/state/nonce validation, issuer/audience/signature/time binding, opaque server-side sessions, rotation, expiry and mixed-credential rejection are required.
controls.limitations: Required by SEC-2; not implemented or tested.

controls.description: Every UI, API, export and job use case must receive trusted context, bind company/owner/object/operation and authorize before disclosure, mutation or side effects.
controls.limitations: No concrete policy matrix or implementation evidence. Decision pass adds React and minimal-attribution rules; deferred event obligations remain blocked.

controls.description: Cookie-authenticated mutations require session-bound CSRF evidence and configured-origin validation; GET/HEAD do not change business state except the validated OIDC callback.
controls.limitations: Exact route mapping and runtime enforcement are absent.

controls.description: Routes must declare authentication, media, byte and pagination bounds, reject unknown/duplicate/invalid fields and use scoped parameterized database access.
controls.limitations: Registered schemas, parsers and SQL do not yet exist.

controls.description: Integration adapters enforce purpose-specific HTTPS destinations, socket-level address validation, redirect revalidation, credentials scope and cumulative byte/time budgets.
controls.limitations: No transport implementation or socket-level test evidence.

controls.description: Repository/source/provider/model content stays data, cannot select execution capabilities, is parsed under finite budgets and crosses retention only after validation/redaction.
controls.limitations: No parsers, workers or adversarial tests exist. Decision pass adds React and minimal-attribution rules; deferred event obligations remain blocked.

controls.description: Credentials stay behind a restricted adapter and AI receives only a final validated allowlisted projection without private identifiers or tools; returned references remain assessment-scoped.
controls.limitations: No captured-byte test exists and audit digest representation is unresolved.

controls.description: One authorized projection drives inert browser/API/export/message output, restricted notes, no-store private responses, authenticated downloads and context-specific CSV/PDF/JSON handling.
controls.limitations: No renderer, headers or output fixtures exist. Decision pass adds React and minimal-attribution rules; deferred event obligations remain blocked.

controls.description: Business change and durable intent commit atomically; jobs retain logical identity, revalidate current authority, fence stale attempts and reconcile unknown external outcomes.
controls.limitations: Queue schema, concurrency behavior and recovery tests are absent.

controls.description: Administrative changes atomically record append-only audit events; the security stream is closed, bounded and redacted, while emission, persistence and delivery remain distinct claims.
controls.limitations: OD-001 through OD-005 block parts of destination, retention, durability and AI-digest enforcement; no runtime coverage. Decision pass adds React and minimal-attribution rules; deferred event obligations remain blocked.

requirements.statement: The release provides a private web application and private API with the same company scope, authorization, validation and content restrictions.
OIDC user/admin roles and personal ownership boundaries govern protected operations; public access and native passwords are excluded.
Repository analysis is read-only except controlled system-owned issue writes, uses immutable evidence, reports gaps and stops on revoked authorization.
Authorized PDF, CSV and JSON exports preserve structured evidence, status, attribution, revision and export time.
Only approved enabled sources may be retrieved and retained with permission, provenance, immutable revisions, validation and visible failures.
External notifications and issues minimize private detail, recheck destination authority, preserve corrections and distinguish provider acceptance from readership.
Durable work survives restarts, preserves event identity, bounds retries and side effects, and exposes progress/failures.
requirements.origin: REQUIREMENTS.md FR-3.19 through FR-3.23, FR-6.7 and NFR-1

requirements.statement: External AI is optional, tool-less and advisory, receives only approved reduced input, and cannot relax local disclosure or matching authority.
Required actions record trusted actor/service, action, time, target, outcome and safe reason under the closed event contract and atomic audit rules.

Every browser, API and worker operation should bind the current principal or service grant, company, function, target object, permitted properties and current resource revision at the decision and effect points.
requirements.origin: REQUIREMENTS.md FR-6.2/FR-6.4/FR-6.7; ARCHITECTURE.md operation-authority contract; SECURITY.md SEC-1/SEC-3

requirements.statement: Export selection, delayed generation, status and download should retain one opaque server-owned identity while rechecking current actor, report revision, archive state and source-use authority before generation and every retrieval.
requirements.origin: REQUIREMENTS.md FR-4.7/FR-6.7; ARCHITECTURE.md reports/views flow; SECURITY.md SEC-7

requirements.statement: Each external adapter should expose a closed typed result whose fields can update only provider-delivery facts; a code-owned use case should exclusively decide business transitions and treat unknown fields or semantics as failure.
requirements.origin: REQUIREMENTS.md FR-10.6; ARCHITECTURE.md delivery/connector contracts; SECURITY.md SEC-8

requirements.statement: Restore should start in quarantine with restored sessions invalid, delayed external effects paused and integrations disabled until current authority, destinations, source rights and credentials are explicitly revalidated.
requirements.origin: REQUIREMENTS.md FR-11.4; ARCHITECTURE.md lifecycle flow; SECURITY.md SEC-6; SECURITY_EVENTS.md SEC-APP-012

requirements.statement: Every high-impact action uses the explicit server-supplied phrase mapping bound to action, target and revision in DESIGN.md.

treatments.outcome: A single operation-authority contract binds the current principal, company, intended request, function, object and permitted input/output properties at every browser and API use case; session recognition alone never grants the operation, and session/role transitions invalidate future operations.
alternatives: Maintain separate UI and API policies with an equivalence proof and shared conformance matrix.
Remove cookie-authenticated mutations and use a separately bounded credential model for all state changes.
tradeoffs: A shared contract reduces drift but requires a complete route/use-case/property inventory.
Frequent current-role checks reduce stale authority but add identity/cache coordination cost.

treatments.outcome: Export request, delayed generation, status and retrieval use one opaque server-owned job/result identity bound to company and report revision; generation and every retrieval recheck current actor, archive state and source-use authority, and invalidated output becomes unavailable without treating identifier possession as authority.
alternatives: Generate and stream exports only inside the authorized request, avoiding retained results.
Use an explicitly bounded delegated export grant with a short documented lifetime and revocation semantics.
tradeoffs: Current reauthorization is strongest for changing rights but may turn a completed job into an unavailable result.
Nonretained streaming simplifies revocation but is less suitable for large asynchronous exports.

treatments.outcome: One code-owned projection keeps source, repository, provider and note content inert in each browser/export context, while private responses and browser state are limited to the currently authorized recipient and cleared or rendered unusable on signout, expiry and role loss.
alternatives: Render untrusted material as plain text only in all privileged views.
Use isolated previews for any future rich content and keep them outside the privileged application context.
tradeoffs: Plain-text rendering reduces interpretation risk but may lose formatting fidelity.
Aggressive client-state clearing improves transition safety but may reduce offline or back-navigation convenience.

treatments.outcome: Each outbound use case owns a closed destination class and minimal data projection, revalidates every permitted redirect and current recipient/source authority immediately before transmission, and cannot reach destinations or send fields outside that contract.
alternatives: Remove runtime-configurable destinations and permit only deployment-fixed endpoints.
Route all outbound traffic through a separately governed egress broker with equivalent purpose and recipient policy.
tradeoffs: Fixed destinations minimize reachability but reduce administrative flexibility.
Immediate rights checks may cancel queued delivery after configuration changes, requiring visible recovery behavior.

treatments.outcome: Every external adapter emits a closed typed local result; only a code-owned use case may map that result to an allowed state transition, acknowledgments record provider facts rather than readership or authority, and unknown or semantically invalid fields fail closed.
alternatives: Discard all provider response bodies and retain only locally observed transport status where business behavior permits.
Use a separate authoritative status channel only if its identity, correlation and transition authority are explicitly modeled.
tradeoffs: Narrow results reduce ambiguity but may omit useful provider diagnostics.
A separate status channel adds integration and correlation complexity and creates another trust boundary.

treatments.outcome: Durable work preserves one logical operation and effect identity, rechecks current authority/resource revision at every external effect and commit, rejects stale competing transitions before effects commit, fences superseded attempts, reconciles unknown outcomes, and remains paused after restore until authority and destinations are revalidated.
alternatives: Serialize each protected business transition so competing attempts cannot reach the effect point.
Reject competing attempts using revision preconditions and permit a separately bounded delegated job grant where current reauthorization is unsuitable.
tradeoffs: Serialization simplifies invariants but reduces concurrency.
Precondition rejection preserves throughput but requires clear conflict UX and retry ownership.
Effect reconciliation may delay completion and depends on provider-observable identities.

treatments.outcome: Every admission, parse, expansion, queue and temporary-output boundary has a documented finite budget and cancellation/failure state, with interactive and durable work isolated sufficiently that excess work is rejected or bounded before shared capacity is exhausted.
alternatives: Accept only precomputed small inputs and disable large asynchronous export or repository operations.
Place heavy work in separately capacity-governed workers while retaining bounded admission at the service.
tradeoffs: Conservative limits protect availability but may reject legitimate large repositories or reports.
Separate worker capacity improves isolation but adds backlog, cancellation and operations complexity.

treatments.outcome: The AI gate constructs and inspects the final serialized outbound bytes from an allowlisted assessment-scoped projection, and returned identifiers are resolved only against the same authorized assessment before any persistence, display or delivery.
alternatives: Disable external AI and retain deterministic local guidance only.
Use an approved self-hosted model behind an equivalent final-byte and reference-resolution boundary.
tradeoffs: Disabling AI removes this egress but reduces advisory capability.
Final-byte capture supports evidence but requires a privacy-safe audit representation, which remains blocked by open decisions.

treatments.outcome: Each required security event has an approved bounded representation, durable write path, consumer and independent silence/health signal; atomic business/audit cases and rolled-back or failed attempts remain distinguishable without claiming that emission, persistence, detection and delivery are equivalent.
alternatives: Keep all security-event obligations blocked until the five open governance decisions are recorded.
Split atomic audit history from an independently durable operational stream while preserving correlation and failure semantics.
tradeoffs: A single durable path is simpler but may not preserve rolled-back attempt evidence.
Separate paths improve failure visibility but require correlation, retention and personal-data governance.

treatments.outcome: Source and repository evidence passes a typed provenance-preserving validation and comparison pipeline that represents malformed, ambiguous, contradictory, incomplete and unsupported states explicitly and cannot collapse them into definite exposure or clean results.
alternatives: Reject any assessment with incomplete evidence and provide no partial result.
Publish partial results only with per-field uncertainty and coverage labels that downstream outputs preserve.
tradeoffs: Whole-assessment rejection is simple but may hide useful supported evidence.
Partial results improve utility but require every renderer and consumer to preserve uncertainty.

treatments.outcome: Every high-impact administrative action displays an exact server-supplied confirmation phrase bound to the current target and revision; the server rejects stale revisions before mutation and a changed target requires a new confirmation and fresh authorization.
alternatives: Use a fresh-auth plus two-person approval workflow for the highest-impact changes.
Use revision-bound review screens with an explicit final action instead of typed confirmation where accessibility evidence supports it.
tradeoffs: Typed phrases create deliberate friction but can burden users and assistive technology.
Two-person approval offers separation of duties but adds organizational and workflow cost.

verification.approach: In a caller-authorized isolated setup, derive an allowed/denied/unknown matrix for two synthetic users, admin operations, objects, properties and cookie/bearer request modes. Compare each allowed route with cross-object, wrong-function, forbidden-property, unintended browser request and post-role-loss cases.
verification.expected_outcome: Every observed route matches the supplied matrix and no session, object identifier or alternate route expands authority.
verification.pass_criteria: All tested allowed cells succeed, all denied cells produce no data or state change, current role loss takes effect, and request/authority observations identify the exact route and operation.
verification.fail_criteria: Any tested denied actor, object, function, property or unintended browser request reads data or changes state, or a stale role remains effective.
verification.inconclusive_criteria: The policy cell is unknown, a route/property inventory is incomplete, or identity, entitlement, request or resulting-state observations are unavailable.

verification.approach: In an isolated setup with synthetic reports and users, observe export request, delayed execution, status and retrieval before and after role loss, archive, source-rights change and result-identifier substitution. Verify 15-minute export expiry, completed-transfer cleanup and fresh authorized regeneration.
verification.expected_outcome: Only a currently authorized actor can cause generation or obtain the result for the bound report revision, and invalidated output is not retrievable by identifier possession.
verification.pass_criteria: The allowed current request succeeds and every tested post-change or substituted identifier path returns no protected bytes and records the defined safe state.
verification.fail_criteria: A currently unauthorized actor generates or receives protected export bytes, or one result identifier resolves across its bound authority/resource context.
verification.inconclusive_criteria: Worker, result-retention, report-revision, current-authority or response-byte observations are unavailable.

verification.approach: Using synthetic inert marker content across every documented rendered field, inspect browser and export outputs and the same private response reuse path for its authorized user, a signed-out client and a later unauthorized browser-profile state after signout or role loss. Include React JSX/prop/URL injection, stale fetch responses, signout/remount/back-navigation, strict CSP and built-client secret leakage.
verification.expected_outcome: Markers remain inert in every context and private content is unavailable to unauthorized or post-transition recipients.
verification.pass_criteria: No marker gains active interpretation, the authorized path remains usable, and no tested unauthorized reuse or browser state exposes the protected content.
verification.fail_criteria: A marker executes or changes privileged context, or protected content reaches a tested unauthorized or post-transition recipient.
verification.inconclusive_criteria: Rendered-field inventory, interpreter context, recipient identity, entitlement, reuse path, storage or response observations are missing.

verification.approach: In a caller-authorized isolated setup, use only inert receivers controlled by the test owner. Exercise every permitted and disallowed destination/redirect transition and compare transmitted fields before and after destination-access or source-rights revocation.
verification.expected_outcome: Only permitted receiver transitions obtain the minimal authorized projection, and changed authority cancels transmission before protected bytes leave.
verification.pass_criteria: All permitted cases reach only the intended inert receiver with allowed fields; disallowed, redirected or revoked cases make no forbidden connection or transmission.
verification.fail_criteria: A disallowed destination/redirect receives a connection or protected field, or a revoked recipient receives output.
verification.inconclusive_criteria: Destination policy, redirect trace, outbound bytes, recipient authority or downstream observation is unavailable.

verification.approach: Against isolated provider doubles, vary only documented acknowledgment, unknown, malformed and business-looking response fields and trace the typed adapter result and every downstream state transition.
verification.expected_outcome: Only schema-valid provider facts update their narrow local delivery/source status; no returned field directly grants authority or changes finding/configuration state.
verification.pass_criteria: Known fields have only their documented effects, unknown/malformed fields fail closed, and no response field bypasses the code-owned transition owner.
verification.fail_criteria: A provider-controlled field changes unauthorized business state, is treated as readership/permission/evidence beyond its contract, or unknown fields are silently authoritative.
verification.inconclusive_criteria: Adapter schema, transition ownership, before/after state or raw-to-typed result observations are unavailable.

verification.approach: In an isolated environment and test sinks, compare delayed work after revocation, two concurrent revision-bound admin changes, retry after an unknown external outcome, a superseded lease and restore with queued effects and integrations present.
verification.expected_outcome: Forbidden or stale effects are stopped before commitment, one logical operation remains correlated across attempts, unknown outcomes reconcile without blind duplication, and restore stays quarantined.
verification.pass_criteria: The documented transition invariant holds at each commitment/effect point, stale attempts cannot commit, external effects do not exceed the permitted count, and no restored session/job/integration resumes before revalidation.
verification.fail_criteria: A revoked/stale/restored attempt performs a forbidden effect, a competing stale mutation commits, an unknown outcome is blindly duplicated, or quarantine is bypassed.
verification.inconclusive_criteria: The business invariant, revision, effect identity, commitment point, provider observation, fence or restore-state evidence is unavailable.

verification.approach: In an isolated capacity test authorized by the caller, exercise documented boundary values and just-over-limit synthetic HTTP, parse, repository, queue and export workloads while observing rejection, cancellation, temporary storage, backlog and interactive service health.
verification.expected_outcome: Every workload is bounded at its declared boundary and excess work fails visibly without unbounded shared-resource growth.
verification.pass_criteria: At-limit cases meet the stated behavior, over-limit cases are rejected or cancelled at the intended boundary, and observed resource/backlog behavior remains within the approved capacity criteria.
verification.fail_criteria: A tested over-limit input bypasses its budget, creates unbounded growth, or prevents required interactive/durable progress beyond the approved criterion.
verification.inconclusive_criteria: A budget, capacity criterion, cancellation trace, resource observation or workload path is unspecified or unavailable.

verification.approach: With a synthetic assessment and controlled AI double, capture the final serialized request bytes and test returned valid, unknown and cross-assessment evidence references before persistence, display and delivery.
verification.expected_outcome: Only allowlisted reduced fields leave, private identifiers/snippets are absent, and only locally valid same-assessment references can influence advice or evidence.
verification.pass_criteria: Captured final bytes match the approved projection and every invalid/cross-assessment reference is rejected without downstream authority.
verification.fail_criteria: A prohibited value appears in final bytes or an invalid/cross-assessment reference is persisted, displayed or delivered as authoritative evidence.
verification.inconclusive_criteria: Final-byte capture, approved field inventory, assessment scope or downstream reference-resolution observations are unavailable.

verification.approach: After OD-001 through OD-005 are decided, inject caller-authorized synthetic success, denial, validation failure, rollback, post-commit failure and telemetry-silence cases and trace schema representation, durable persistence, consumer handling and independent health detection.
verification.expected_outcome: Each required case has its defined record and consumer outcome, while absence/silence is detected independently and no claim conflates emission with persistence or alert delivery.
verification.pass_criteria: Every required synthetic case is durably represented and consumed according to the approved contract, rollback semantics are distinguishable, and silence triggers the independent health signal within its approved bound.
verification.fail_criteria: A required case cannot be represented/persisted/consumed, a rollback creates a false success record, or telemetry silence remains indistinguishable from health.
verification.inconclusive_criteria: Any governing decision, expected record, durable-store observation, consumer trace or health bound remains unavailable.

verification.approach: Using synthetic source/repository fixtures with malformed, ambiguous, contradictory, truncated, unsupported and complete evidence, trace validation, comparison, finding state and every output projection.
verification.expected_outcome: Only fully supported cases become definite; every other fixture retains its precise uncertainty or fails visibly without becoming clean.
verification.pass_criteria: All fixtures produce their predeclared evidence state, provenance remains attached, and no incomplete or failed path emits an unsupported definite or clean result.
verification.fail_criteria: Any malformed/ambiguous/incomplete fixture becomes definite or clean, loses material provenance, or silently overwrites a prior supported finding.
verification.inconclusive_criteria: Expected fixture outcomes, parser/comparator trace, finding revision or output observations are unavailable.

verification.approach: In an isolated UI/API setup, open a high-impact confirmation for one target revision, then change the target or revision before submission and compare with an unchanged authorized submission, including keyboard and assistive-technology interaction.
verification.expected_outcome: Only the unchanged currently authorized target/revision can commit, exact confirmation remains perceivable and operable, and stale state requires a new phrase and fresh review.
verification.pass_criteria: The current unchanged case commits with matching audit, while every stale/changed case produces no mutation and presents a safe recoverable conflict requiring reconfirmation.
verification.fail_criteria: A stale phrase or revision commits, the confirmation can target a different record than displayed, or the mutation and audit disagree.
verification.inconclusive_criteria: The exact phrase mapping, current revision, resulting state, audit record or accessibility observation is unavailable.

decisions.rationale: Keep risks unrated until deployment and implementation evidence supports a named rubric and meaningful business impact; blocks rating claims only.
Retain full pipeline coverage gate; OD-003 resolved, OD-001/002/004/005 deferred with owners. No emission/consumer coverage claimed.
Adopt DESIGN.md per-action exact revision-bound phrases; runtime V-011 remains not_run.
